system: English common law; judicial review of legislative acts limited to matters of interpretation

constitution.amend: proposed by the National Assembly; passage of amendments to constitutional articles including those on sovereignty of the United Republic, the authorities and powers of the government, the president, the Assembly, and the High Court requires two-thirds majority vote of the mainland Assembly membership and of the Zanzibar House of Representatives membership; House of Representatives approval of other amendments is not required

courts.highest: Court of Appeal of the United Republic of Tanzania (consists of the chief justice and 14 justices); High Court of the United Republic for Mainland Tanzania (consists of the principal judge and 30 judges organized into commercial, land, and labor courts); High Court of Zanzibar (consists of the chief justice and 10 justices)
courts.judges: Court of Appeal and High Court justices appointed by the national president after consultation with the Judicial Service Commission for Tanzania, a judicial body of high-level judges and 2 members appointed by the national president; Court of Appeal and High Court judges serve until mandatory retirement at age 60, but terms can be extended; High Court of Zanzibar judges appointed by the national president after consultation with the Judicial Commission of Zanzibar; judges can serve until mandatory retirement at age 65
courts.lower: Resident Magistrates Courts; Kadhi courts (for Islamic family matters); district and primary courts

citizenship.descent: at least one parent must be a citizen of Tanzania; if a child is born abroad, the father must be a citizen of Tanzania

world: has not submitted an ICJ jurisdiction declaration; accepts ICCt jurisdiction
